## Dispatch order — R34

Claimed by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_012CZgmFFzqA9cX8tBMhvpFe`. Branch: **`claude/issue-6409-node-version-recogniser`**. Assignee is this seat's shared identity — the claim is this comment plus the session ID.

### The ruling you are executing (triage, 2026-08-25T21:49:57Z — verbatim)

> Queue charter adopted from the card: ⛔ not a `SEP` widening (established impossible by the earlier spelling card); a **second recogniser** for the `name-version: N` shape or an alias list treating `node-version` as a spelling of the Node toolchain; then triage every literal the widened scan surfaces (⛔ no bulk `KNOWN_CLAIMS` additions to get green); and the permanent fixture test that rebuilds the pre-fix recogniser and asserts it fails on the line the new one matches — the corpus no longer contains a live instance, so without that fixture a revert is unobservable.
>
> **Hot-file serial:** this file is also the surface of PR #6401 (in flight) and of #6400 (queued this same round, different defect form — anchor-prose drift). Fold-or-serial answered: **serial** — the two cards fail the same-defect-same-fix fold gate. Claim order: after PR #6401 lands, then these two in either order but never concurrently.

⭐ **The serial constraint is satisfied**: PR #6401 merged at **20:41:46Z**. ⛔ **#6400 is NOT dispatched and must not be** while you hold this — it is a different defect form on the same file (anchor-prose drift, not recogniser blindness). Do not touch its `KNOWN_CLAIMS` reason string.

⛔ Type is **Bug**, not Task: the ledger's own declared promise — *"every literal is either exempt or inventoried"* — silently does not hold for the canonical Node spelling. Declared ≠ enforced.

### ⛔ Three closed doors, so you do not spend time re-opening them

1. **`SEP` cannot fix this.** #6307 established the shape of the limit: `_Node.js_` stays invisible whatever goes in the character class, because `\b` fires on neither side of a word character. Here the obstacle is **a word** (`version`), not a separator character. ⚠️ Widening `SEP` to admit `[a-z]` would make it match almost anything and destroy the gate.
2. **No bulk `KNOWN_CLAIMS` additions to get green.** An entry written to silence a gate is worse than the blind spot it replaces.
3. **Do not delete the offending literals to pass.** #6308 already removed the only live `node-version: 20`; deleting is not the fix here, seeing is.

### The two shapes the ruling allows — pick one and argue for it

- **A second recogniser** for the `name-version: N` shape, or
- **an alias list** treating `node-version` as a spelling of the `Node` toolchain.

Say which you chose and why. ⚠️ Whichever you pick, be explicit about what it does **not** cover — the two neighbouring spellings on the card (`actions/setup-node@v4`, `pnpm/action-setup@v4`) are action pins rather than toolchain floors, and I am **not** asking you to cover them. If your recogniser happens to catch them, say so and triage what it surfaces; if it does not, say that too.

### ⭐ The fixture is the part that will decay without care — build it first

`#6308` deleted the corpus's only live `node-version: 20`. So after your fix, **reverting your recogniser changes nothing observable** and the blind spot returns unnoticed. This is exactly the trap #6307 hit and closed.

Copy its shape: a permanent test that **rebuilds the pre-fix recogniser** and asserts it **fails** on the same line the new one matches — the two side by side, in one test. ⛔ A test that only asserts the new recogniser works is not enough; it goes green under a revert if the corpus has no instance.

Prove it in both directions: revert your recogniser, run, record **RED**; restore via `git checkout HEAD -- <absolute path>` under `trap … EXIT INT TERM`, prove the restore by `git hash-object` matching and an empty `git diff HEAD`, re-run **GREEN**.

### Then triage what the widened scan surfaces

Each new hit is a real claim to inventory **or** an exemption with a stated reason. ⚠️ Report the decision for **each one** with its reason. ⭐ And show the gate output **before and after** — blind → seeing. A recogniser change with no observable difference in what gets scanned is not a fix, and this is the one gate whose entire defect is reporting green over what it never examined.

### Constraints

- ⛔ **Worktree-first**: `git worktree add ../objectui-6409 -b claude/issue-6409-node-version-recogniser main && cd ../objectui-6409 && pnpm install`.
- ⛔ **Never `git stash`** — the stack is shared across every worktree of this repo.
- ⛔ **Never touch `content/docs/releases/`.**
- ⛔ Do not set `domain:*` or type labels; file findings **unassigned**.
- ⚠️ Every zero-hit needs a **control term** — a string you know is present, matched by the same sweep. This lane has been defeated three times today by readings taken without one.
- ⚠️ Run the **whole** `scripts/__tests__` tree.
- Changeset required. Open the PR as **draft**; this seat arms it.

### Reporting

Structured JSON report: which shape you chose and why, what it does not cover, before/after gate output, the per-literal triage decisions, and the two-direction fixture evidence with hashes.

Context you should not re-litigate: this card exists because I asserted on #6308 that the gate *"skips fences by design"*. It does not — the file's own header says fences are scanned on purpose. The dev on #6308 re-measured and found the real cause. ⛔ Do not inherit the fence explanation from anywhere it still appears.

### Per-literal triage (the one hit the widened scan surfaces)

**`content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md :: node-version: 20` → inventoried `anchored`.** Not deleted, not bulk-added.

The line is prose in the "Adding a New Workflow" section: *"a hardcoded `node-version: 20` where every workflow declares `'22.x'` (and 20 sat below the floor the root `package.json`'s `engines` field now declares)"*. It is **not a version this page teaches** — it cites `node-version: 20` as the value the page's own copied YAML block had fossilised at, and states in the same breath that every workflow declares 22 instead. Deleting it would delete true, useful documentation, which is why it is inventoried rather than repaired.

Anchor re-measured against `.github/workflows` at this cut: **28 `node-version` declarations across 23 files, ZERO reading 20, all 28 reading 22** (control, same sweep: 19 `corepack enable` steps). The surrounding claim holds too — root `engines.node` is `>=22.11`, so 20 does sit below the declared floor. The sentence goes false exactly when the workflows move off 22, which is when it should.

The entry's `why` deliberately carries **no declaration count**, because counts in this ledger's reason strings are exactly what #6400 is open about.

### Noted, not acted on, not re-filed

#6400's premise is corroborated and has drifted further since it was filed: the `Node 22.x` entry's reason names 14 declarations, #6400 measured 27, I measure **28 across 23 files** (27 reading `'22.x'`, one reading `'22'`). Per the serial ruling I did **not** touch that entry or its reason string. Nothing new filed — this is already that card.

One thing I checked and deliberately did **not** file: the `check-vi-mock-specifiers: the population COLLAPSED` banner printed during the tree run is the *expected output* of that file's own `it('exits non-zero on a collapsed population, with the census in the message')`, which drives `main()` against an empty file list on purpose. It appears identically in the BASE run. Not a defect.

## Review — ACCEPT (PR #6429). ⭐ It refuted one of the two ruled options instead of choosing between them.

Reviewed by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_012CZgmFFzqA9cX8tBMhvpFe`, R34.

### The shape choice is a measurement, not a preference

Triage offered two shapes — a second recogniser, or an alias treating `node-version` as a spelling of `Node`. ⭐ **The alias shape cannot see the literal that produced this card**, and the dev proved it rather than picking on taste:

`TOOLCHAIN` feeds the claim regex whose value pattern is `VERSION`, and `VERSION` **deliberately refuses a bare integer** — the file's own comment records why: a bare-integer rule reads `| coerceCell | Vitest | 100% |` as *"Vitest 100"*. Measured on the alias shape: `node-version: '22.x'` matches, `node-version: 20.11.1` matches, and **`node-version: 20` — this card's own literal — does not.** Buying it back would mean loosening `VERSION` for **every** claim in the file: the exact widening that file already measured and rejected.

A keyed recogniser carries its own value pattern, legal only inside that shape *because the key declares what the value is*, and `VERSION` is untouched. ⭐ It also keys the claim on the whole shape with the quote closed by a backreference, instead of handing the key whatever `SEP` consumed — the `@vitejs/plugin-react` pathology the file already records.

### ⚠️ It corrected my premise, and the correction is mine to own

I wrote on this card, and repeated in the dispatch order, that #6308 removed the corpus's only live instance. **False.** `content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md:1744` still carries `node-version: 20` in **prose**, citing the value the page's own fossilised YAML had drifted to. So a revert is observable on the corpus today as well as through the fixture.

⛔ That does not make the fixture optional, and the dev says why: **that prose can be reworded out of existence by any docs PR**, and then the corpus instance is gone again. The fixture is the durable witness. ⭐ Keeping it for the right reason after the stated reason turned out to be wrong is better than keeping it because I said so.

### The discarded control is the detail I most want on the record

> my first corpus sweep used `engines.node` as its control and it returned **ZERO** — that control was **INVALID and was discarded, not reported**; it was replaced with `Node 22.x` (3 hits) and the workflow sweep with `corepack enable` (19 hits).

⭐ A control that returns zero is not a control — it is a second unexplained absence. Noticing that, throwing it away, and **saying so** is precisely the discipline this lane has failed at three times today. ⛔ The quiet version of this is to report the zero-hit anyway and call it measured.

### Boundaries verified, not assumed

`actions/setup-node@v4` and `pnpm/action-setup@v4` produce **no** claim after the change — their obstacle is `@`, a separator **character**, so a `SEP` question and not this one — and both are pinned as boundary assertions. `python-version:` / `java-version:` / `go-version:` are out because the key prefix must be a `TOOLCHAIN` name and this tree states no version for those runtimes (measured zero, control: one `node-version:` line). The spaced prose spelling `Node version 20` is out, measured zero with a control — recorded as a boundary the way #6307 recorded underscore emphasis.

### The per-literal triage, and one restraint worth naming

The single new hit is **inventoried `anchored`, not deleted** — correctly: the line is true documentation, citing `node-version: 20` as the value the page's own copied YAML had fossilised at while stating in the same breath that every workflow declares 22. Anchor re-measured at this cut: **28 declarations across 23 files, zero reading 20**, control `corepack enable` × 19.

⭐ And the entry's `why` **deliberately carries no declaration count**, *"because counts in this ledger's reason strings are exactly what #6400 is open about."* That is refusing to create the neighbouring defect while fixing this one.

⛔ #6400's reason string was **not touched**, per the serial ruling — though the measurement corroborates it and shows further drift: the entry says 14, #6400 measured 27, this measures **28 across 23 files**. That belongs on #6400, not here.

### Evidence

Whole tree 81 files / 2318 tests (base 2317 — the +1 is the fixture). Census before/after over 241 files: 37 → 38 matched, **one new, none lost**. Blind→seeing shown through the gate's own output. Two-direction ablation with the HEAD blob compared to disk **before** mutating (proving the right tree was measured), mutation proved by anchored marker counts, restore proved by hash match and empty `git diff HEAD`, and ⭐ the ablated run reddened **both** the new fixture and the ratchet's *"no entry may outlive the claim it excuses"* — which is the second, independent witness.

### Disposition

⛔ Arming on **every** check green. Not governed surface. Arms when CI is clean.
